title: Turn a school calculator keys up in its slide cover: draw it out, hand it over and roll it in the air, slide it back in
instruction: Take the slide cover off the front of the calculator and slide it onto the back, so that the calculator lies keys up in its cover.
context: A scientific calculator's hard slide cover protects its keys in a school bag; during a lesson it goes on the calculator's back, so that the calculator lies keys up in it and the cover is not lost. Pupils with a Texas Instruments TI-30XIIS do this at the start of a lesson. The cover is a stiff channel closed at one end, its side lips running in grooves along the calculator's sides: it cannot be pressed on from above. Here the calculator lies keys down in its cover on a notebook, the cover underneath. Neither part is fixed: one hand holds the loose cover in line against the click (about 6 N; 9 N pushing home in the reference run) while the other draws the calculator out and later pushes it home, and in between the calculator is handed from hand to hand and rolled keys up in the air, since the robot hand's level grip, the one that can roll it, needs 54 to 74 mm clear below its grip point. Its end must enter the cover's open end within about half a millimetre and a degree.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x away from the arms, y to the left); heights over the bench top. Notebook: a closed A5 hardback of any make, light grey, 21.0 x 14.8 x 1.5 cm (a), lying flat, its long side along y, its middle at x 24, y 4, taped to the bench with double-sided tape on marks at its four corners. Calculator: Texas Instruments TI-30XIIS, navy, 15.5 x 8.1 x 1.9 cm, 100 g (a), lying KEYS DOWN in its slide cover on the notebook, along y, its middle at x 24, y -4.75: the cover underneath, channel up, over the keys; the cover's open end (the calculator's display end) to the right (-y), 6.0 cm past the notebook's right edge; its closed end at the ON-key end. Cover: 'Ti-30XIIS Scientific Calculator Slide Cover' (Underwood Distributing), black (also sold in navy), or the slide cover the calculator is sold with, measured; 15.65 x 8.44 x 1.31 cm, 30 g (a); home: the calculator's end against its end wall, clicked in. Pencil: Staedtler Noris HB, yellow, along y beside the notebook, its middle at x 34.4, y 5, taped to the bench with double-sided tape on marks at its two ends (for the desk's look). Both arms in their ready pose. Nothing varies by seed.
scoring: The end state counts, except 'came off the front' and 'left the bench', which hold over the whole trial and are checked from the trial video. 1.0: the calculator lies keys up in its cover with the cover on its back, home (its end within 3 mm of the cover's end wall: a rule laid along the side; it clicked), lying flat (within 10 degrees), calculator and cover at rest, both grippers 3 cm or more from them. 0.5: the cover on the calculator's back rails, the calculator keys up and at least 40 mm into them (a rule), the other 1.0 conditions not all met. 0.25: the cover came off the front at some moment and is not on the front rails at the end, the 1.0 and 0.5 conditions not met. 0: the cover on the front rails at the end, or the calculator or the cover left the bench at any moment. A trial ends once 1.0 has held 5 s.
reset_notes: About 15 s: slide the calculator back into the cover keys first, over its keys, until it clicks; lay the pair on the notebook cover down, its long side along y, the open end 6.0 cm past the notebook's right edge (a mark on the notebook's side) and its middle over the notebook's middle line (within 3 mm); notebook and pencil on their marks; check with a photo from above against the start picture. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid parts at true size (sizes assumed until measured: README). The cover's lips are real shapes in real grooves; once a lip is 6 mm in within the rails' play (0.5 mm across, 0.6 mm up or down at its leading end, 1 degree) the calculator is set on the rail line and slides on a joint: 1.5 N to slide and 6 N to click in or out (assumed), read every 50 ms. The plastic's flex is not modelled.
